2608.01711.title: Constructing Executable Analytical Knowledge Representations for Meta-Analysis Synthesis Using an Agentic Harness
2608.01711.paper_summary: Meta-analysis synthesis highlights a fundamental challenge in knowledge-based scientific analysis: structured evidence does not by itself represent the analytical knowledge required for executable computation. Decisions about evidence assignment, analytical contrasts, outcome and time-point alignment, effect-size formulation, and methodological admissibility must be explicit before statistical execution. Existing automated approaches often embed these decisions in model outputs, generated code, or workflow traces rather than representing them as independently verifiable knowledge. We introduce the Executable Analytical Knowledge Representation (EAKR), a machine-actionable representation of the knowledge required to transform structured evidence into executable meta-analysis. An EAKR represents evidence, relations, numerical inputs, constraints, provenance, and unresolved issues. We operationalise EAKR in MetaSynDec, an agentic harness in which large language models propose structured updates and deterministic services govern schema- and contract-based validation and execution. Across 58 synthesis units, MetaSynDec constructed all EAKRs, with 57 proceeding to statistical execution. Of 56 units with sufficient information to define a reference analysis object, 38 (67.9%) achieved complete object fidelity and 42 (75.0%) exact evidence-set agreement, with a mean Jaccard similarity of 0.909. Generated and published confidence intervals overlapped in 54 of 55 units (98.2%). MetaSynDec outperformed direct LLM generation in reference synthesis-structure agreement (57/58 versus 23/58; p<0.001) and among 23 jointly completed units, exact reference-formulation agreement (23/23 versus 1/23; p<0.001). These findings provide feasibility evidence that EAKR supports formal validation, traceability, statistical execution, and improved methodological agreement relative to direct LLM generation.
2608.01711.paper_summary_zh: Meta-analysis synthesis highlights a fundamental challenge in knowledge-based scientific analysis: structured evidence does not by itself represent the analytical knowledge required for executable computation.<lb/>關於證據分配、分析對比、結果和時間點對齊、效應大小公式及方法學可接受性的決策必須在統計執行之前明確。<lb/>現有的自動化方法通常將這些決策嵌入模型輸出、生成的代碼或工作流程追蹤中，而不是將其表示為可獨立驗證的知識。<lb/>我們引入了可執行分析知識表示（EAKR），這是一種可機器操作的表示，旨在將結構化證據轉化為可執行的元分析所需的知識。<lb/>EAKR表示證據、關係、數值輸入、約束、來源和未解決的問題。<lb/>我們在MetaSynDec中將EAKR進行操作化，這是一個代理性工具，其中大型語言模型提出結構化更新，而確定性服務則管理基於架構和合同的驗證與執行。<lb/>在58個綜合單位中，MetaSynDec構建了所有EAKR，其中57個進行了統計執行。<lb/>在56個擁有足夠信息以定義參考分析對象的單位中，38個（67.9%）實現了完整的對象保真度，42個（75.0%）達成了精確的證據集一致性，平均Jaccard相似度為0.909。<lb/>生成和發布的置信區間在55個單位中有54個（98.2%）重疊。<lb/>MetaSynDec在參考綜合結構一致性方面超越了直接LLM生成（57/58對23/58；p<0.001），在23個共同完成的單位中，精確的參考公式一致性（23/23對1/23；p<0.001）。<lb/>這些發現提供了可行性證據，表明EAKR支持正式驗證、可追溯性、統計執行以及相對於直接LLM生成的改進方法學一致性。
